Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide on-grid invariant

## Summary
Replace the hard-coded fire-rate constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` with values derived from the 80 BPM beat period. Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates derived from beat period.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — invariant test.

## Risks
- Low: existing tests will verify no unintended behaviour changes. The rapid weapon (125 ms) is unchanged; cannon, spread, and dual rates change slightly.
data.title: Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant

data.description:
Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.
data.title: Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Make the default BPM, per-weapon subdivisions (or fire-rate multiples), and quantisation behaviour configurable through the projects existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/constants.ts`). Include sane defaults. Tests must assert a config override changes the firing cadence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — BPM is configurable through the existing rules/config system with a default of 80.
- [ ] **AC2** — Per-weapon subdivisions (or fire rates) are configurable through the same system.
- [ ] **AC3** — Config overrides are tested: changing BPM or a subdivision changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC4** — No scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals — all values come from the config or are derived from it.
- [ ] **AC5** — The config system handles corrupt/missing config gracefully, falling back to defaults.
- [ ] **AC6** — Subdivisions are configured as positive integers and each fire rate is derived from the beat period, so the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant (parent AC3) holds by construction; a test asserts the invariant under a non-default config.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC4** — [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.

## Key Files
- `src/core/rules.ts` or `src/core/constants.ts` — configurable BPM + subdivisions.
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — reads config for BPM.
- Tests for config override → cadence change.

# Goal

Verify the audit-runner fixes satisfy all parent acceptance criteria, add regression coverage, and confirm the full project test suite passes.

# Background

The parent work item (AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV) has 5 acceptance criteria. AC1 (fingerprint scoping) appears already implemented in `_compute_content_fingerprint` — this task must verify it, and close any remaining gap. AC2-AC3 are implemented by the sibling task. AC4 (no regression on interactive runs) and AC5 (full test suite passes) are verified here.

# Verification tasks

## 1. Verify AC1 — fingerprint scoping

Confirm `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger. The existing tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` (`TestContentFreshnessGate`) should prove:
- `test_fingerprint_does_not_query_bare_head` — the whole-repo HEAD sha is not a fingerprint input
- `test_fingerprint_stable_for_unrelated_commit` — an unrelated commit leaves the fingerprint unchanged

If any gap remains (e.g. a bare `git rev-parse HEAD` call still leaks in), fix it.

## 2. Verify AC2/AC3 — in-main-slot partial handling and diagnostics

Add/verify tests that:
- A parent audit with children whose ACs are `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot work reports "Ready to close: Yes" (when parent ACs are met)
- The audit JSON output includes the `children_assessment` diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot children from genuine-not-ready children
- A genuine `partial`/`unmet` child verdict still blocks the parent (regression guard)

## 3. Verify AC4 — no regression on interactive runs

Add/verify tests that:
- In-main-slot mode (`child_in_main_slot=True`) with a serviced child (verdicts parsed as `met`) still honours the full in-main-slot workflow
- Separate-process mode (`child_in_main_slot=False`) is unchanged
- Existing `test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` tests continue to pass

## 4. Verify AC5 — full project test suite

Run the complete project test suite (`/skill:test`) and confirm zero failures. Triage any failures into critical `test-failure` work items per the triage policy.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: `_compute_content_fingerprint` is confirmed (by test) to exclude the global HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger
- AC4: Interactive/separate-process audit behaviour is unchanged (regression tests pass)
- AC5: Full project test suite passes with zero failures
- New tests exist that prove AC2 and AC3 behaviour (unserviced in-main-slot partials do not block; diagnostic distinguishes them)

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — fingerprint tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — implementation under test
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite runner

# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `explodeRandom`, RNG seam, mineral field.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — docstring/behaviour.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — shared helper (from the previous task).

## Summary

Add the unmistakable, screen-wide Phase Shift "juice" as one shared, toggleable module (parent AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8). Per producer answer Q4: a subtle screen desaturation/dim plus a chromatic split-tint applied to on-screen enemies, bullets and minerals, a light camera shake on activation, all driven for the duration of the effect and cleanly cleared on expiry; the existing ship ghost alpha is retained. The visual layers are individually toggleable (mirroring `playerDeathJuice`) so tests can assert state transitions.

## Why

Auto-trigger is only trustworthy if the player can see it fire. A single shared module keeps the game and gyms visually identical and guards against the scope creep called out in the parent's risks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC4.1 — A new pure-parameter + Phaser-rendering module `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` owns the effect; no per-scene copies of the treatment exist.
- [ ] AC4.2 — On activation the module applies: desaturation/dim, chromatic split-tint on enemies/bullets/minerals, and a light camera shake; the ship keeps its ghost alpha via the existing `applyPhaseGhost()`.
- [ ] AC4.3 — Each layer has an exported enable toggle (mirroring `playerDeathJuice`); disabling a layer removes only that layer.
- [ ] AC4.4 — The effect is driven by the phase duration and is **cleanly cleared on expiry** (no residual tint/shake), and is a safe no-op when the player/scene is absent.
- [ ] AC4.5 — A crisp activation is impossible to miss: the treatment begins on the same frame Phase Shift activates.
- [ ] AC4.6 — Unit tests assert the parameter model and layer on/off + clear transitions; rendering uses the existing Phaser test stubs so headless tests do not break.
- [ ] AC4.7 — `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass; new tests fail against the pre-change implementation.

- [ ] Traceability — parent AC5 (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8): [ ] **AC5 — Juice and audio.** On every Phase Shift activation, all on-screen enemies, bullets and minerals receive the shared phase visual treatment (fade/shake and/or global distortion) for the duration of the effect and it is cleanly cleared on expiry; the ship ghost remains. A dedicated sci-fi Phase Shift WebAudio cue plays on activation and degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext. The visual layers are toggleable (mirroring `playerDeathJuice`) and unit-tested for state transitions; audio presence is asserted via the existing audio-test seams.


## Minimal Implementation

- Create `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` following the `playerDeathJuice.ts` shape (exported tunables, pure resolver, `spawnPhaseShiftJuice`/`update`/`clear` composition).
- Call it from the shared activation site (C3) so every scene inherits it; keep rendering out of `src/powerups`.
- Add `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (new)
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` (new)
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` (pattern reference)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on **C3** (needs the shared activation hook).

# Tests: asteroid-independent wave completion and persistence

Parent: AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO (bug, high).

## Goal / User story

As a tester, I want deterministic tests that assert a wave completes as soon as
the enemy ships are gone (regardless of live asteroids), and that asteroids and
minerals persist across wave/level transitions, so the new wave rule cannot
silently regress.

This is the **test-first** work item for the parent bug: write/adjust the tests
so they encode the new rule and fail (red) against the current, old-rule code.

## Scope

Update the tests that currently assert the old rule and add new coverage:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`:
  - Replace `AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed`.
  - Replace `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5 — carried-over asteroids are re-registered…`.
  - Update the asteroid-integration accounting assertions that expect a split
    child / released asteroid to increment `enemiesAlive` (approx. lines 1232,
    1257).
  - Update the asteroid-spawner integration assertion that a released asteroid
    increments `enemiesAlive` (approx. lines 2327, 2349).
  - Add: wave clears with live asteroids present; `enemiesAlive` excludes
    asteroids and split children; asteroids persist across a wave transition
    and across a level transition; timeout does not re-register asteroids;
    minerals persist across a transition; boss-entry clearing still destroys
    carried-over asteroids.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`: re-frame the "dynamic spawn registration"
  suite as the generic seam (drop the asteroid-semantics claim); keep the API
  tests, because the API is retained.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Wave completion ignores asteroids — test: the wave clears while non-asteroid
  enemy ships are destroyed even when asteroids remain alive, and
  `WaveManager.enemiesAlive` excludes them.
- Minerals persist — test: minerals already on the field remain in place across
  wave and level transitions.
- Boss entry keeps clearing asteroids — test: carried-over asteroids are still
  destroyed when the boss encounter begins.
- Tests updated and comprehensive — unit/integration tests cover wave clearing
  with live asteroids, `enemiesAlive` excluding asteroids and split children,
  persistence across wave and level transitions, and timeout not re-registering
  asteroids.
- A test asserts a released offscreen asteroid and a split child do not
  increment `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`.
- A test asserts surviving asteroids remain alive and continue to move after a
  wave transition and after a level transition.
- A test asserts a surviving asteroid is not re-registered on wave timeout (for
  example, `enemiesAlive` after timeout equals the next wave's enemy-ship
  count).
- All added/updated tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no wall-clock waits)
  and fail (red) against the pre-change code.
- The rest of the suite still runs with no unrelated failures; the new/updated
  tests fail only on the old-rule assertions.

## Minimal Implementation

- Use the existing PlayScene test harness helpers (`findAsteroids`, the
  `wm` accessor, the wave-timeout helper).
- Assert directly on `WaveManager.enemiesAlive` and scene alive counts; avoid
  timing-based waits.
- Title replaced tests with the parent id, e.g.
  `AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC1 — wave clears with live asteroids`.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — replace/extend the wave-accounting and persistence tests.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — re-frame the dynamic-spawn suite.

## Dependencies

- None (first item).

## Deliverables

- Red (failing) tests encoding the new rule.
- A comment listing every replaced/added test.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --run` (the repo's standard vitest invocation) shows the new
  tests failing only on the old-rule assertions.

# Stop registering asteroids with the WaveManager

Parent: AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO (bug, high).

## Goal / User story

As a player, I want a wave to complete as soon as the enemy ships are gone, so
drifting asteroids do not stall my progress. As a developer, I want wave
accounting expressed in one place so it cannot drift between game and tests.

Asteroids must no longer influence `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`; they persist in
the field across wave and level transitions as classic-Asteroids debris.

## Scope note (extra call site)

The parent brief's predicted Key Files list two registration sites
(`_spawnScheduledAsteroid`, `_splitAsteroid`) plus the timeout re-registration.
Repository research found a **fourth** production call site:
`PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt(x, y, sizeTier)` (public helper used by tests and the
mineral gym) also calls `registerDynamicSpawn(1)`. It is spawned-asteroid
registration and must be removed too, or asteroids placed through it would
still gate the wave.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Wave completion ignores asteroids — when all non-asteroid enemies in the wave
  are destroyed it clears regardless of how many asteroids remain alive, and
  `enemiesAlive` excludes asteroids and split children.
- Asteroids persist — surviving asteroids remain alive in the scene across wave
  and level transitions, with motion, wrapping, rotation and shootability
  unchanged.
- Split behaviour preserved (gameplay only) — destroying a large/medium
  asteroid still spawns exactly two smaller children at its position with
  divergent directions; the split no longer registers a dynamic spawn.
- Wave-timeout unchanged for ships — on wave-timeout every surviving
  non-asteroid enemy still detonates at 10x scale and costs exactly one life;
  surviving asteroids are not re-registered and remain alive and persistent.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- `PlayScene._spawnScheduledAsteroid`, `PlayScene._splitAsteroid` and the public
  `PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt` no longer call `registerDynamicSpawn`.
- `PlayScene._timeoutWave` no longer re-registers surviving asteroids (the
  `survivingAsteroids` re-registration block is removed).
- No production code path registers asteroids with the `WaveManager`; a grep of
  `src/` (excluding `*.test.ts`) finds no asteroid `registerDynamicSpawn` call
  site.
- `registerDynamicSpawn` / `unregisterDynamicSpawn` remain on `WaveManager`
  (kept as a general dynamic-spawn seam) with a doc comment clarifying that
  asteroids are not registered; `_enemiesAlive` semantics are unchanged.
- Code comments in `PlayScene` (scheduled spawn, split, timeout and
  `spawnAsteroidAt`) state that asteroids are not wave-accounted and persist
  across transitions.
- `_clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry` is unchanged and still destroys carried-over
  asteroids on boss entry.
- The tests from the preceding test-first item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Delete the four `registerDynamicSpawn(...)` calls in `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Delete the surviving-asteroid re-registration block in `_timeoutWave` and the
  now-unused `survivingAsteroids` local.
- Update the related JSDoc/comments in `PlayScene` and the `WaveManager` doc
  comment for the dynamic-spawn seam.
- Do **not** touch the shared split helper (`src/scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`)
  or the gyms.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove asteroid dynamic-spawn registration and update comments.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — clarify the dynamic-spawn seam doc comment.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the test-first item (tests must be red first).

## Deliverables

- Asteroid-free wave accounting in `PlayScene`.
- Passing tests from the test-first item plus the existing suite.

## Verification

- `grep -rn registerDynamicSpawn src/ --include=*.ts` shows only `WaveManager`
  and `*.test.ts` references.
- `npm test -- --run` is green.

# Curve generator: per-wave generation-mode control with read-only derived difficulty

## Goal

As a **designer**, working in the Dev Utilities curve generator (gym scene), I want a per-wave **generation-mode** control (`curve` | `fixed` | `dynamic`, default `curve`) so I can set each wave's behaviour from the editor. When I choose `fixed`, the difficulty slider must be **read-only** and show the difficulty **derived from that wave's current settings**.

## Context / existing state

- Curve editor/preview scene — `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), surfaced under **Dev Utilities** on the gym index.
- Each wave is a row with a 0–100 target slider (`data-curve-wave`), a value readout (`data-curve-wave-value`) and a Remove button; the panel has Add Wave and Regenerate, and an edit-to-clear stale state (`CURVE_PREVIEW_STALE_TEXT`).
- The generation-mode capability it exposes is delivered by the sibling item *Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration*. This item is the UI only; it must not reimplement the mode engine.

## Desired behaviour

- Each wave row gains a labelled mode control with exactly three options — `curve`, `fixed`, `dynamic` — defaulting to `curve`.
- Selecting `fixed`:
  - the target-difficulty slider becomes read-only/disabled;
  - the slider/readout shows the difficulty **computed from the wave's current (fixed) settings**, not an editable target;
  - the value is clearly presented as derived (e.g. a "fixed" affordance/label), not user-editable.
- Selecting `curve` or `dynamic` re-enables the editable target slider.
- Changing a wave's mode counts as an edit and marks the preview stale (existing edit-to-clear behaviour).
- Regenerate reflects the mode: `curve` and `dynamic` previews come from the sequencer; a `fixed` wave previews its authored composition and its derived difficulty.
- Mode choices must be persisted/reported through the same config path as the other wave fields (so the editor and the shipped CSV agree) — the exact persistence is shared with the sibling engine item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every curve row renders a generation-mode control offering `curve`, `fixed` and `dynamic`, defaulting to `curve`.
- Choosing `fixed` disables the target slider and displays the difficulty derived from the wave's current settings; the value cannot be edited through the slider.
- Choosing `curve` or `dynamic` re-enables the target slider and it is editable again.
- Changing a mode marks the preview stale and clears the wave list until Regenerate is pressed.
- Regenerating shows sequencer-derived previews for `curve`/`dynamic` waves and the authored composition plus derived difficulty for `fixed` waves.
- The control is keyboard accessible and labelled (no slider-dependent-only interaction).
- Unit/DOM tests (`GymCurveSequencer.test.ts`) cover default mode, the `fixed` read-only derived-difficulty behaviour, re-enabling, and the stale transition.
- The full suite passes.

## Out of scope

- The mode engine, CSV schema and runtime behaviour (sibling *Per-wave generation modes…* item).
- Saving/loading curves to the shipped CSV beyond what already exists; visual formation previews; drag-to-reorder.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — mode control, read-only derived slider, preview wiring.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts` — DOM/behaviour tests.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` / `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — consumed read-only for the derived difficulty.

## Goal

## Context

It depends on the generation-mode engine, the curve-generator UI and the retuned default curve.

## Desired behaviour

- Flip the default: `DEFAULT_SEQUENCED_WAVES_ENABLED = true`; `DEFAULT_RULES.sequencedWavesEnabled === true` and `cloneDefaultRules()` agrees.

# Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability

## Goal

As a **player**, the default (seeded) campaign should ramp difficulty smoothly and feel engaging, so enabling sequenced generation does not degrade the early game.

## Problem

The seeded default curve was derived mechanically from the static level measurements (see `defaultDifficultyCurves()` in `src/core/configStore.ts:114`). Measured evidence from the builder at HEAD `819429a` shows the generated campaign is degenerate in early levels:

| Level | Static | Generated (current defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Entry | `scout x6`, `scout x8` | `asteroid x1`, `asteroid x1` |
| 2 Descent | `scout x8`, `diver x8`, `swarm x10` | `asteroid x1`, `asteroid x1`, `scout x1` |
| 3 The Core | `tank6+scout4`, `diver6+scout4`, `tank6+swarm10` | `scout x1`, `scout x1`, `scout x1` |
| 4 Firestorm | `diver x6`, `tank x6`, `swarm x10` (fire) | `scout x18`, `swarm x15`, `diver x6` (fire) |
| 5 Predictable Death | `phaser x4`, `phaser x5` (fire) | `tank x1`, `phaser x4` (fire) |

Low early targets make the sequencer select the cheapest archetype (the non-firing asteroid) or a single-count group, so levels 1–3 are sparse and unengaging.

## Desired behaviour

- Retune the default difficulty curve (and, where appropriate, use the `fixed` generation mode from the sibling item for onboarding waves) so the default campaign:
  - removes degenerate early waves (no asteroid-only and no 1-count waves in levels 1–3);
  - keeps targets non-decreasing and within 0–100;
  - ramps smoothly across and within levels, preserving an intentional fire boundary (levels 1–3 do not fire; 4+ do);
  - yields wave compositions comparable in spirit to the hand-authored `LEVELS` (varied archetypes, sensible counts) while still being curve-driven where intended.
- Ensure the default campaign covers every configured level/wave with a playable composition and no empty/duplicate rows.
- Validate through the curve-generator preview and/or an automated spawn-plan assertion, not only by eye.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The default generated campaign contains **no** `asteroid`-only wave and **no** 1-count wave in levels 1–3 (test asserts on `buildSequencedLevels()` output / `WaveManager.planSpawns()`).
- Default target difficulties are non-decreasing within each level and across levels and stay within 0–100.
- Every configured wave yields a non-empty composition; aggregated difficulty increases from level 1 to the final level (no reversals).
- The fire boundary holds: levels 1–3 `shootEnabled=false`, levels 4+ `true`.
- The default curve is derived/stored consistently: `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` agree, and codec/seed tests pass.
- A regression test pins the improved default campaign so a future change cannot silently reintroduce degenerate early waves.
- The full suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration* (so early onboarding waves can be `fixed` and the rest tuned against the new modes).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `defaultDifficultyCurves()` target values.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — seeded campaign targets/modes.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — default/seed assertions.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — default campaign regression assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — preview used for validation.
